lines.text: Flip a coin eight times. Will the same side come up three times in a row?
lines.caption: Flip a coin eight times. Will the same side come up three times in a row?

lines.text: Most people guess that's rare. <short pause> But it happens almost three times out of four!
lines.caption: Most people guess that's rare. But it happens almost three times out of four!

lines.text: Hi there, I'm Vantee! Let's count how often it does NOT happen.
lines.caption: Hi there, I'm Vantee! Let's count how often it does NOT happen.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: A fair coin is flipped eight times.
lines.caption: A fair coin is flipped eight times.

lines.text: What is the probability that the same side never comes up three times in a row?
lines.caption: What is the probability that the same side never comes up three times in a row?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: Let's break it down. Each flip is heads or tails.
lines.caption: Let's break it down. Each flip is heads or tails.

lines.text: Each flip doubles the choices, so eight flips give two hundred fifty-six outcomes.
lines.caption: Each flip doubles the choices, so eight flips give two hundred fifty-six outcomes.

lines.text: This outcome is good. No side comes up three times in a row.
lines.caption: This outcome is good. No side comes up three times in a row.

lines.text: This outcome is bad. It has three heads in a row.
lines.caption: This outcome is bad. It has three heads in a row.

lines.text: Three tails in a row is just as bad.
lines.caption: Three tails in a row is just as bad.

lines.text: Every outcome is equally likely, so count the good ones and divide by two hundred fifty-six.
lines.caption: Every outcome is equally likely, so count the good ones and divide by two hundred fifty-six.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

scenes.chapter: Solution 1: build it flip by flip

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's start small, and build up one flip at a time.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's start small, and build up one flip at a time.

lines.text: A streak is a run of the same side, like these two heads.
lines.caption: A streak is a run of the same side, like these two heads.

lines.text: We'll call each outcome a string. In a good one, every streak is one or two flips long.
lines.caption: We'll call each outcome a string. In a good one, every streak is one or two flips long.

lines.text: With one flip, there are two good strings. With two flips, all four strings are good.
lines.caption: With one flip, there are two good strings. With two flips, all four strings are good.

lines.text: Now three flips. A string can end with a single: one flip of the other side, added to a good two-flip string.
lines.caption: Now three flips. A string can end with a single: one flip of the other side, added to a good two-flip string.

lines.text: It has to be the other side, or that streak would get longer.
lines.caption: It has to be the other side, or that streak would get longer.

lines.text: Or it can end with a double: two flips of the other side, added to a good one-flip string.
lines.caption: Or it can end with a double: two flips of the other side, added to a good one-flip string.

lines.text: Four plus two gives six good strings. Only the two triples are missing!
lines.caption: Four plus two gives six good strings. Only the two triples are missing!

lines.text: The same rule works for every length.
lines.caption: The same rule works for every length.

lines.text: Each count is the one before it, plus the one before that.
lines.caption: Each count is the one before it, plus the one before that.

lines.text: Four plus six is ten. Six plus ten is sixteen.
lines.caption: Four plus six is ten. Six plus ten is sixteen.

lines.text: Then twenty-six, forty-two, and finally sixty-eight!
lines.caption: Then twenty-six, forty-two, and finally sixty-eight!

lines.text: So sixty-eight of the two hundred fifty-six outcomes are good.
lines.caption: So sixty-eight of the two hundred fifty-six outcomes are good.

lines.text: Sixty-eight over two hundred fifty-six simplifies to seventeen over sixty-four.
lines.caption: Sixty-eight over two hundred fifty-six simplifies to seventeen over sixty-four.

lines.text: That's Choice D, about twenty-seven percent!
lines.caption: That's Choice D, about twenty-seven percent!

lines.text: Here's a second way. Let's cut a good outcome into its streaks.
lines.caption: Here's a second way. Let's cut a good outcome into its streaks.

lines.text: This one is a double, a single, a double, another double, and a single.
lines.caption: This one is a double, a single, a double, another double, and a single.

lines.text: Write the lengths as blocks. Together they cover all eight coin flips.
lines.caption: Write the lengths as blocks. Together they cover all eight coin flips.

lines.text: Now go backwards. Pick the blocks, and pick the first side.
lines.caption: Now go backwards. Pick the blocks, and pick the first side.

lines.text: The sides must take turns, so the whole string is fixed!
lines.caption: The sides must take turns, so the whole string is fixed!

lines.text: So we count the block patterns, then double it, for heads or tails first.
lines.caption: So we count the block patterns, then double it, for heads or tails first.

lines.text: Let's sort the patterns by how many doubles they have.
lines.caption: Let's sort the patterns by how many doubles they have.

lines.text: No doubles means eight single blocks. That's just one pattern.
lines.caption: No doubles means eight single blocks. That's just one pattern.

lines.text: One double makes seven blocks. The double can go in any of the seven places.
lines.caption: One double makes seven blocks. The double can go in any of the seven places.

lines.text: With two doubles, we have six blocks. Pick two of the six to be doubles.
lines.caption: With two doubles, we have six blocks. Pick two of the six to be doubles.

lines.text: There are six choices for the first double, and five for the second.
lines.caption: There are six choices for the first double, and five for the second.

lines.text: But that counts each pair twice. Half of thirty is fifteen ways.
lines.caption: But that counts each pair twice. Half of thirty is fifteen ways.

lines.text: Three doubles make five blocks. Pick two singles: five, then four. Half of twenty is ten ways.
lines.caption: Three doubles make five blocks. Pick two singles: five, then four. Half of twenty is ten ways.

lines.text: Four doubles: just one pattern.
lines.caption: Four doubles: just one pattern.

lines.text: One plus seven plus fifteen plus ten plus one is thirty-four patterns.
lines.caption: One plus seven plus fifteen plus ten plus one is thirty-four patterns.

lines.text: Double it for the first side: sixty-eight good strings again. It matches!
lines.caption: Double it for the first side: sixty-eight good strings again. It matches!

lines.text: Here's a fun surprise. Count the patterns for shorter strings.
lines.caption: Here's a fun surprise. Count the patterns for shorter strings.

lines.text: You get the Fibonacci numbers! Each one is the sum of the two before it.
lines.caption: You get the Fibonacci numbers! Each one is the sum of the two before it.

lines.text: Double them, and you get the table from Solution 1.
lines.caption: Double them, and you get the table from Solution 1.

lines.text: So when would you pick each way? The table is fastest for long strings.
lines.caption: So when would you pick each way? The table is fastest for long strings.

lines.text: The blocks show WHY it works, and make a great double-check.
lines.caption: The blocks show WHY it works, and make a great double-check.

lines.text: Choice B is thirty-four over two hundred fifty-six. It forgets the first side.
lines.caption: Choice B is thirty-four over two hundred fifty-six. It forgets the first side.

lines.text: Choice E only stops three heads in a row. It still counts strings like this, with three tails.
lines.caption: Choice E only stops three heads in a row. It still counts strings like this, with three tails.

lines.text: Choice A, one over eight, is the chance that three given flips are all heads. Wrong question!
lines.caption: Choice A, one over eight, is the chance that three given flips are all heads. Wrong question!

lines.text: Choice C, one over four, is the chance that three given flips all match. Also the wrong question.
lines.caption: Choice C, one over four, is the chance that three given flips all match. Also the wrong question.

lines.text: So here's a great habit: check the rule for BOTH sides, and count every starting choice.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit: check the rule for BOTH sides, and count every starting choice.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? This time, flip the coin nine times.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? This time, flip the coin nine times.

lines.text: What is the probability that the same side never comes up three times in a row?
lines.caption: What is the probability that the same side never comes up three times in a row?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. The table only needs one more step.
lines.caption: Let's check. The table only needs one more step.

lines.text: Forty-two plus sixty-eight gives one hundred ten good strings in all.
lines.caption: Forty-two plus sixty-eight gives one hundred ten good strings in all.

lines.text: Nine flips give five hundred twelve outcomes, double the last time.
lines.caption: Nine flips give five hundred twelve outcomes, double the last time.

lines.text: So the probability is one hundred ten over five hundred twelve.
lines.caption: So the probability is one hundred ten over five hundred twelve.

lines.text: Divide both numbers by two, and it's fifty-five over two hundred fifty-six!
lines.caption: Divide both numbers by two, and it's fifty-five over two hundred fifty-six!

lines.text: Check with blocks: one plus eight plus twenty-one plus twenty plus five is fifty-five patterns.
lines.caption: Check with blocks: one plus eight plus twenty-one plus twenty plus five is fifty-five patterns.

lines.text: If you found fifty-five over two hundred fifty-six, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you found fifty-five over two hundred fifty-six, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: Cut each outcome into streaks, and count the patterns of streak lengths.
lines.caption: Cut each outcome into streaks, and count the patterns of streak lengths.

lines.text: Then multiply by two, for heads or tails first.
lines.caption: Then multiply by two, for heads or tails first.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
